thread:
Alex C.: FYI Acme support escalated — their embeddings endpoint started returning dimension errors and high latency after traffic shifted regions around 09:12 UTC. They say it worked fine earlier.
Maria L.: Can you paste the exact error they see?
Alex C.: "Embedding creation failed: dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 768)" — plus lots of 5xx spikes and requests routed to us-east-1 even though their tenant is pinned to eu-west-1.
Jordan P.: Ugh. That combination screams a model variant mismatch during routing fallback. If routing sent requests to a smaller model with 768 dims we'll see that.
Alex C.: I collected headers and sample payloads. They call our embeddings endpoint with model: "open-embed-1536" and region eu-west-1. Request ID: r-ACME-20260312-091234\. Attached logs (pasted):
```
[09:11:58] incoming request tenant=acme region=eu-west-1 model=open-embed-1536
[09:12:01] route_decision: eu-west-1 -> eu-west-1 (pool=embed-1536-a)
[09:12:05] route_decision: eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 (pool=embed-768-b) fallback=capacity_spillover
[09:12:06] serve_error: dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=768 req=r-ACME-20260312-091234
[09:12:07] http 500 resp body: {"error":"dimension mismatch"}
```
Maria L.: That log line is gold. It says fallback=capacity_spillover — meaning the routing layer forwarded to a compatible model but wrong dimensionality. Jordan, is there a known mapping bug where fallback picks a smaller embedding model and doesn't convert dims?
Jordan P.: There isn't supposed to be an automatic downcast. Our route policy should only select compatible variants (same dim) or use an internal adapter to pad/convert. Looks like routing allowed a different model family. I'll check the policy rules for tenant pins.
infra-oncall: Investigating routing tables for eu-west-1. I'm seeing high contention on pool embed-1536-a around 09:12, autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough, spillover policy triggered to us-east-1 pools.
Alex C.: Client also reported billing anomalies — they saw doubled usage for a 2-minute window (Billing Bot flagged it). Possible duplicate retries because of 500s?
Billing Bot: Alert: tenant=acme usage spike +135% between 09:12-09:14 UTC; likely retries.
Maria L.: Repro steps request from Acme: they ask for a minimal repro that we can run. I created a curl using their exact model param.
```
curl -X POST "https://api.eu-west-1.redwood.com/v1/embeddings" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["test sentence"]}'
```
I ran it in our eu-west test env and saw a 200 with 1536 dims. Running it with low concurrency and forcing capacity_spillover predicate via a simulate header triggers the mismatch.
Jordan P.: Can you share the simulate header you used?
Alex C.: I used `X-REDWOOD-SIMULATE-SPILLOVER: true` in the request; it forced routing to a us-east pool. Then we saw the 500 with dimension mismatch.
Jordan P.: Ok that repro is deterministic. Looks like the routing metadata isn't checking embedding dimension compatibility when evaluating cross-region fallbacks. I'll open a quick PR to add dim check to the policy matcher. In the meantime, recommended workaround: tenant pin to region with `pin_region=true` which bypasses spillover, or set a fallback model mapping (`fallback_model:on-mismatch`) to a conversion adapter.
Maria L.: Acme is on a production plan and can't afford double-billing or 5xx. Can we hotfix faster? Maybe a routing rule rollback to disable cross-region spillover for embeddings until patch?
infra-oncall: I can flip a feature flag to disable spillover for the embeddings route group for tenant-scoped requests. That will keep requests queued or 429 instead of routing to mismatched pools. Rolling it now (will take ~2 minutes).
support-bot: Deploy started by infra-oncall. Change: routing.feature.spillover.embeddings -> false (target: eu-west-1).
[~2 minutes later]
support-bot: Deploy succeeded. infra-oncall: Spillover disabled for embeddings in eu-west-1. We should monitor 500s and latency.
Alex C.: I asked Acme to retry now. They reported immediate success — no dimension errors and normal latency restored. Billing Bot: anomaly reduced; no more duplicate spikes.
Jordan P.: I'll push a small validation change to the routing service that enforces dimension match when considering fallback pools. Will include unit tests and an emergency migration script to backfill any routing table entries missing the dim tag.
Maria L.: Timeline to prod fix?
Jordan P.: PR in ~30m, can cut a hotfix canary and roll within 2 hours if no regressions.
Alex C.: For customer communication: I'm drafting an incident note indicating root cause: cross-region spillover routed to incompatible embedding pool (dim mismatch) because routing matcher lacked explicit dim compatibility check. Mitigation: spillover disabled for embeddings. Permanent fix: routing validation + adapter or model mapping.
Maria L.: Also include repro steps and a snippet so customers can test after we enable any fallback. Add guidance to pin region or add fallback_model in their tenant config for short-term.
infra-oncall: I'll also add a warmup job for embedding pools when autoscaler sees sustained queue growth to avoid cold starts causing spillover.
Alex C.: Thanks team. I'll escalate pace with Acme and keep them updated. If anyone sees related threads from other tenants, ping me. :thumbsup:
Jordan P.: Follow-up: PR #4821 opened with validation and tests. I'll post link when CI completes.
support-bot: CI passed for PR #4821. Staging hotfix canary scheduled.
infra-oncall: Canary deploy to staging succeeded. Planning prod hotfix in 45 minutes during low-traffic window.
Alex C.: Great. Closing interim support loop; will update thread after prod hotfix and customer confirmation.
